What we know on day 1,719

Prefer the Guardian on Google Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused Russia of intensifying strikes across the country to put pressure on Kyiv at upcoming talks after an overnight barrage triggered power cuts as temperatures drop. “By intensifying its attacks on Ukraine and our infrastructure at this very moment, Russia is trying to additionally lay the groundwork for putting pressure on Ukraine’s position and that of its partners,” the Ukrainian president said. “Russia perceives diplomacy in its own peculiar way – as a form of aggression.”

Ukraine’s energy ministry said “a massive attack on a number of energy facilities” on Saturday had plunged five regions into darkness and significantly hampered electricity transmission in Kyiv and surrounding regions. Russia had throughout the night launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, Zelenskyy said, among which were KN-23 missiles manufactured and supplied by North Korea.

The strikes came before a US-brokered trilateral meeting in Abu Dhabi scheduled for next week aimed at reviving stalled diplomatic efforts towards peace. Ukrainian officials are expected to sit down with Russian negotiators and US envoys on Tuesday and Wednesday for the first such talks in months. The diplomatic track has been stalled since February when Washington shifted attention to its war with Iran.

The National Guard’s 1st Azov Corps later admitted the building belonged to one of its units and was being used to hold newly mobilized soldiers and men who had gone AWOL. Four men were sent to hospital with injuries. A doctor who entered the building alleged that one had a broken spine. Kyrylo Budanov arrived at the scene, where a 14-year-old boy was filmed being escorted out wrapped in a blanket. On November 3, Ukraine’s State Bureau of Investigation opened criminal proceedings over possible abuse of authority by military officials. The National Guard says it will no longer use the building. Budanov says investigators will identify those behind the clashes, while the question of who authorized the detention site and what happened to the men inside remains unanswered.

Accusations that men were being beaten and held for money brought furious relatives to its gates while senior officials scrambled to respond.

The confrontation has exposed a darker side to Kiev's military recruitment system, already notorious for men being dragged off the streets. It has also revived questions about secret detention and torture facilities documented in Ukraine long before the latest scandal.
Who was being held, how did they get there, and what have their military superiors admitted? Here is what we know.
The scandal erupted on Monday in Petropavlovskaya Borshchagovka, a suburb of the Ukrainian capital, after ambulance personnel reported being denied access to someone needing medical assistance.

According to the IDF, Abu Saeed held hostage Omer Shem Tov in captivity for 505 days. Shem Tov was later released as part of a hostage deal.

In separate strikes, six terror operatives from Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, and the Army of Islam were killed near Khan Yunis.

article.title: Israel says killed senior Hamas intelligence official in Gaza
article.description: JERUSALEM, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- Israel's military and Shin Bet security agency said Wednesday that they had killed a senior Hamas intelligence official .....
paragraphs: JERUSALEM, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- Israel's military and Shin Bet security agency said Wednesday that they had killed a senior Hamas intelligence official in an airstrike in Gaza City on Sunday.

In a joint statement, they identified the man as Jamal Abu Saeed, head of operations in Hamas' military intelligence apparatus, saying he had held Israeli hostage Omer Shem Tov captive during the war.
The statement accused Abu Saeed of planning attacks against Israeli troops and civilians and attempting to rebuild Hamas' military capabilities in violation of the ceasefire.
There was no immediate confirmation from Hamas.

Since the ceasefire between Hamas and Israel took effect in October 2025, Israeli attacks have killed 1,602 people, bringing the total death toll since Oct. 7, 2023, to 74,618, according to Gaza-based health authorities on Wednesday.

article.title: Israeli Strike on Tents in Gaza City Park Kills 17-Year-Old Girl
article.description: A 17-year-old girl was among at least four Palestinians killed by Israeli strikes in Gaza on Tuesday, as the Israeli military continues its constant violations of the US-backed ceasefire deal. The girl, identified as Rimas al-Madhoun, was killed when an Israeli drone struck tents in a park in Gaza City,…
paragraphs: A 17-year-old girl was among at least four Palestinians killed by Israeli strikes in Gaza on Tuesday, as the Israeli military continues its constant violations of the US-backed ceasefire deal.

The girl, identified as Rimas al-Madhoun, was killed when an Israeli drone struck tents in a park in Gaza City, Gaza’s civil defense spokesman Mahmoud Bassal told AFP . Sources told the Anadolu Agency that several Palestinians were wounded by the strike on the tent camp, and some were in critical condition.

In Khan Younis, southern Gaza, an Israeli strike on a car killed at least three Palestinians, including a member of the Gaza Interior Ministry’s internal security services. In a statement , the Interior Ministry identified the victim as 44-year-old First Khaled Ibrahim Muhammad Shallouf.

“He was killed as a result of an Israeli bombing that targeted a number of officers and members of the Internal Security Service in the al-Mawasi area of ​​Khan Yunis city this afternoon,” the ministry said.

The strike came two days after an Israeli bombing killed at least six police officers in southern Gaza. The Interior Ministry described the strikes as “part of the ongoing series of Israeli crimes against the security and police system in the Gaza Strip, in an effort to spread chaos within Palestinian society.”

Credit: IDF. (Nov. 2, 2026 / JNS) The Israel Defense Forces said on Monday that it had eliminated four Hamas terrorists in a series of strikes in the northern Gaza Strip.
Two strikes on Saturday eliminated Nabil Hamad, a department head in Hamas’s recruitment apparatus, and Mohannad Nader Mahmoud Dahdouh, a sniper commander, the military said.

Two strikes on Oct. 22 eliminated Wael Naif Fahmi Muslim and Arafat Kamal Muhammad Ar’air. Muslim was a Nukhba Force terrorist who infiltrated Israel during the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas massacre. Ar’air was a squad commander in Hamas’s rocket array.

The IDF said the four had advanced attacks against troops and civilians and worked to restore Hamas’s capabilities “in systematic violation of the ceasefire.” Precision munitions and aerial surveillance were used to limit harm to noncombatants, it added.
IDF soldiers remain deployed in the Gaza Strip in accordance with the Oct. 10, 2025, U.S.-brokered ceasefire deal, according to the IDF.

Hormozgan Province Deputy Governor for Political, Security and Social Affairs Ahmad Nafisi confirmed that the unprovoked aggression occurred at approximately 11:30 a.m. local time.
The incident occurred about 18 nautical miles off the coast of Masan village, a coastal settlement in Qeshm County.
According to the deputy governor, the two fishing vessels each had two crew members aboard when they were attacked by American forces.
Following the assault, two fishermen were rescued and taken back to Qeshm. One suffered injuries in the attack and was transferred to a local hospital for treatment.
